title: FFI surface for Kotlin and Swift
summary: Expose the core to both apps via UniFFI
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing built. Depends on the rule model, expander and geocoder phases being in place.

Expose the core through UniFFI so Kotlin (Android) and Swift (iOS) call one implementation. Rust was chosen over Kotlin Multiplatform partly because its C ABI also reaches HarmonyOS Node-API if Huawei is ever taken on.

SURFACE TO EXPOSE:
  normalize(raw, defaultRegion) -> E164
  evaluate(E164, RuleSet) -> Allow | Block | Silence | Label(text)
  geocode(E164, language) -> Country / Region / City | NotGeographic
  expand(Rule, limit) -> streaming sorted numbers | TooBroad(count)
  explain(Rule) -> expansion count + per-platform verdict
  dataset version accessors, for R5 diagnostics

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS SET BY THE CALLERS:
- The iOS Call Directory extension streams potentially millions of numbers under tight memory limits. expand must NOT return a materialised list across the FFI boundary — design for incremental yield or callback, and verify the chosen shape does not defeat it.
- evaluate runs on the call path on Android and inside the iOS SMS extension. Keep it allocation-light and avoid loading the whole dataset to answer one question.
- Both apps must be able to open a dataset without parsing raw XML at runtime (see F003).

GENERATION IN CI, NOT CHECKED IN: bindings are generated during the build (F006), never committed, or they drift from the core.

THREADING AND ERRORS: decide how errors cross the boundary and what happens on a corrupt or partially applied dataset. Per F003, the evaluator must never see a half-applied dataset.

TESTABILITY: test the generated bindings from both Kotlin and Swift, not just the Rust side — the boundary is where the shapes above actually get proven.
